card.one_liner: Schedule-change refund rights, pricing the new flight before quoting a fee, and why you never cancel a round trip.

rules.text: Basic economy tickets are non-refundable and non-changeable under the fare rules.
Quote the change fee and the fare difference together, never the fee alone.
A round trip is changed, never cancelled, when the customer only wants to drop the return.
Missed flights are rebooked under same-day standby when available.

exceptions.text: An airline schedule change over 2 hours gives a full refund regardless of fare class; about one booking in eight qualifies and the airline will not volunteer it.
Some carriers use 90 minutes and one uses 3 hours for the schedule-change threshold; keep a per-carrier line.
A hotel non-refundable rate can be moved by date once by calling the property directly, roughly half the time; prepaid wholesaler rates cannot.
For cancellations after 9 pm, check interline partner flights before the airline's own rebooking options.

judgment_calls.text: A 'denied boarding' claim is checked against the gate time in the record; arriving after gate close is a missed flight, and filing it as denied boarding can void travel insurance.
Partner protection only works on the operating carrier's ticket stock; agency-issued tickets go back to the agency, adding a day.
If the new flight is cheaper than the fee, present the credit explicitly; most customers never use an unexplained credit.

common_mistakes.text: Quoting a 200 dollar change fee to move to a flight that is 150 dollars cheaper, without pricing the new itinerary.
Cancelling a round trip when the customer wanted to drop only the return, forfeiting the outbound.
Missing a qualifying schedule change because only the current time was checked.

never_do.text: Never file a missed flight as denied boarding to trigger compensation; refuse and use the standby rule, usually a 75 dollar fee.
Never cancel a round trip to drop a return.
Never quote a change fee before pricing the new flight.
